title: Spreading a given chart of a fine log stalk
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $M\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$ be a fine log structure: it is a log structure as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] admitting etale-local charts by finitely generated integral commutative monoids, without requiring saturation; integral means that the monoid embeds in its group completion. Let $\bar x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], let $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $M_{\bar x}$ be the geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and let $P$ be a finitely generated integral commutative monoid. Suppose $h:P\to M_{\bar x}$ is a monoid homomorphism and, writing $E=(\alpha h)^{-1}(A^\times)$, the induced homomorphism
$$P\oplus_E A^\times\longrightarrow M_{\bar x},\qquad [p,u]\longmapsto h(p)u$$
is an isomorphism. Here the pushout identifies $e\in E$ with its image $\alpha h(e)\in A^\times$, as in the chart definition [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Then there is an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-etale-morphism] and a chart $\widetilde h:P\to M|_W$ whose germ is the specified homomorphism $h$ under the canonical stalk identification $M_{\bar w}\cong M_{\bar x}$.

proof.text: Use a small skeleton of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods: affine etale objects form an essentially small category, and the possible lifts of the fixed geometric point to each object form a set. Affine neighbourhoods are cofinal for stalks, and pointed neighbourhoods are cofiltered; affine refinements of their common sources and equalizers show that the opposite of this skeleton is filtered. For any finite family of sheaves, stalks are their section colimits. Commutation with finite products and equalizers implies the following finite-data rule: finitely many germs have representatives on one common pointed neighbourhood, and finitely many equations between these representatives which hold as germs hold after a further pointed refinement. All later refinements use this rule, allowing the several sheaves to be $M$, $\mathcal O$ or an associated log sheaf. Every such neighbourhood is locally Noetherian: an etale morphism is locally of finite presentation, whose affine polynomial quotient presentations show it is locally of finite type, and the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma applies to its map to $X$. Neighbourhoods factoring through a fixed pointed etale neighbourhood compute the same stalk: a common refinement with any other neighbourhood exists by cofilteredness, and parallel arrows can be equalized there. Thus subsequent stalk identifications preserve the specified germs.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating tuple $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ of $P$. The finite-presentation lemma supplies finitely many defining relations for this tuple. Represent each $h(p_i)$ by a section of $M$ on a common pointed neighbourhood. Each defining relation holds at the specified stalk because $h$ is a homomorphism; impose the finitely many relations by step 1. The presentation's universal property now gives a homomorphism $\widetilde h:P\to M(U)$ with precisely the germ $h$. By fineness of $M$, refine once more to a pointed etale neighbourhood admitting a chart $q:Q\to M(U)$ with $Q$ finitely generated and integral. Such a refinement exists because an etale chart covering has a member through the geometric point, and that member is itself pointed by a lift of the geometric point. No saturation or freeness is assumed for either $P$ or $Q$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69 and 75: agent expansion of the omitted chart-extension argument.

proof.text: Put $\beta=\alpha\widetilde h$ and let $N=L_U(P,\beta)$, with canonical generator map $\iota:P\to N(U)$. The associated-log universal property extends $\widetilde h$ uniquely to a homomorphism $f:N\to M|_U$ over the identity of $U$. By its stalk formula, $N_{\bar u}=P\oplus_E A^\times$, and $f_{\bar u}$ is exactly $[p,u]\mapsto h(p)u$. The hypothesis of the item says this map is an isomorphism. In particular its inverse fixes $A^\times$ and is compatible with the structure maps to $A$. This proves a stalk assertion only; an inverse on a neighbourhood will be constructed in the next steps.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69 and 75: agent expansion of the omitted chart-extension argument.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating tuple $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$ and finitely many defining relations using the finite-presentation lemma. For each $q_j$ take $n_j=f_{\bar u}^{-1}(q(q_j)_{\bar u})\in N_{\bar u}$, and represent these by sections $t_j$ of $N$ on a common pointed refinement. At the stalk, these sections satisfy every defining relation of $Q$, as well as the finitely many equations $\alpha_N(t_j)=\alpha_M(q(q_j))$ in $\mathcal O$ and $f(t_j)=q(q_j)$ in $M$. The relations hold because $f_{\bar u}^{-1}$ is a monoid homomorphism compatible with the structural maps. Impose all these equations simultaneously by the finite-data rule of step 1. The resulting tuple defines a homomorphism $k:Q\to N(V)$ with $\alpha_N k=\alpha_M q$ and $fk=q$. The identities on the finite generators imply the displayed identities on all of $Q$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69 and 75: agent expansion of the omitted chart-extension argument.

proof.text: Since $q:Q\to M|_V$ is a chart, the chart form of the associated-log universal property extends $k$ uniquely to a log homomorphism $g:M|_V\to N|_V$. Both $fg$ and the identity of $M|_V$ restrict to $q$ on $Q$, since $fk=q$. Uniqueness in that same universal property gives $fg=\mathrm{id}_{M|_V}$. This equality is on the whole neighbourhood, including its unit sheaf; no finite generation of the unit groups is asserted.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69 and 75: agent expansion of the omitted chart-extension argument.

proof.text: At the marked stalk, $f_{\bar v}$ is the isomorphism of step 3. Taking stalks in $fg=\mathrm{id}$ therefore gives $g_{\bar v}=f_{\bar v}^{-1}$ and $(gf)_{\bar v}=\mathrm{id}$. Consequently, for each of the finitely many $p_i$ from step 2, the two sections $gf(\iota(p_i))$ and $\iota(p_i)$ of $N$ have equal germs. Refine once more so that all these equalities hold as sections, using step 1. They then hold for every $p\in P$ by generation. Uniqueness in the universal property of $N=L(P,\beta)$ shows $gf=\mathrm{id}_N$. Thus $f$ and $g$ are inverse isomorphisms on this neighbourhood. The map $P\to M$ is a chart because its induced associated-log homomorphism $f$ is an isomorphism, and its germ is still the originally specified $h$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69 and 75: agent expansion of the omitted chart-extension argument.

proof.text: Finally take an affine pointed etale refinement $(W,\bar w)$ using cofinality of affine neighbourhoods. The restriction compatibility of associated log structures restricts the two inverse maps, so $P\to M|_W$ remains a chart. Step 1 identifies its marked stalk canonically with $M_{\bar x}$, and every generator has the original germ $h(p_i)$; hence the whole monoid homomorphism has germ $h$. This gives the affine pointed neighbourhood and the specified chart required in the statement.

A chart for a fine log structure at a geometric stalk spreads to a chart on a pointed etale neighborhood.

Sources: Travaux de Gabber VI 1.1 (printed p.69; log structures are étale, fine/fs means étale-local charts) and VI 3.7(a) (printed p.75; 'la restriction de s à Q est, au voisinage de x, une carte'). The item statement is unchanged and not weakened; the full germ h is kept, which the parent lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart needs. Steps: 1 sets up the finite-data rule correctly from the cofiltered, essentially-small, affine-cofinal and filtered-colimit nodes, and gets local Noetherianity from étale => lfp => lft => 01T6. 2 spreads h using the monoid presentation, then gets a fine chart through x̄ from the étale-cover lift. 3 uses the associated-log stalk formula to show f at x̄ is the hypothesis isomorphism. 4 lifts the Q-generators with the Q-relations and f(t_j)=q(q_j); the α equation is redundant but harmless. 5 builds g from the chart form of the universal property, and uniqueness gives fg=id. 6 gets gf=id from generator germs and uniqueness for N, which is a real two-sided inverse; the chart condition then holds stalkwise. 7 makes the neighbourhood affine. New node lem-trf-fg-commutative-monoid-finite-presentation is Rédei's theorem: true, and the 00FN binomial-kernel route is sound; tested on n=0, Z/2, the idempotent monoid 2p=p and repeated generators. New node lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks is Kato's associated log structure: the construction, log axiom, universal property, stalk formula, restriction and chart clauses are all correct; tested on R=N with beta(1)=t at t=0 and t≠0, and on R a group. Both are statement only and self-contained. Duplicate search (rg over the DAG; the log nodes of sec-trace-formula; blueprint main-20261015) found nothing, so same_as=[] is right. Neither restates an item clause and there is no cycle. I accept both tool_uses: the affine-cofinal lemma is Lean-closed and the étale-cover lift is a Mathlib leaf. No route departure. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem EtaleLogStructure.exists_affine_chart_of_isStalkChart {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (M : EtaleLogStructure X) (hM : ∀ (Ω' : Type u) [Field Ω'] [IsAlgClosed Ω'] (t' : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ X), ∃ (V : X.Etale) (_v : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t').fiber.obj V) (Q : Type u) (_ : CommMonoid Q) (q : Q →* M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op V)), Monoid.FG Q ∧ Function.Injective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := Q)) ∧ M.IsChart V q) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) {P : Type u} [CommMonoid P] (hPfg : Monoid.FG P) (hPint : Function.Injective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := P))) (h : P →* M.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalk t) (hh : M.IsStalkChart t h) : ∃ (W : X.Etale) (w : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t).fiber.obj W) (hW : P →* M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op W)), IsAffine W.left ∧ M.IsChart W hW ∧ (M.toEtalePrelogStructure.germ t W w).hom.comp hW = h
